events.did: stood before the penthouse windows watching the crimson spill across the skyline and decided it was going to be a good day
events.quote_anchor: June stood before the penthouse windows, watching the crimson spill across the skyline, and decided it was going to be a good day.

events.did: applied the rosy polish to her toenails and wiggled them, saying aloud that she liked the shade
events.quote_anchor: Then wiggled her freshly painted toes. “I like this shade,” she said aloud. No one answered.

events.did: read the name on the bottom of the polish bottle and judged the color was more a Summer Blush, a Tip of the Tongue pink
events.quote_anchor: It was more a Summer Blush, she thought, a Tip of the Tongue pink.

events.did: rose from the sofa when her phone chimed, wincing at the shallow pain as she stepped around the body on the floor
events.quote_anchor: June sighed, and rose, wincing at the wave of shallow pain as she stepped around the body on the floor.

events.did: discovered that her body only heals while she is wearing it, though she had been shot more than a year ago
events.quote_anchor: It had been more than a year since she’d been shot, but June had since discovered, much to her chagrin, that her body only healed while she was wearing it.

events.did: found the dead man sitting upright in the entry way, shot in the crotch, the heart and the head
events.quote_anchor: the man sitting upright in the entry way, slumped against the wall where he’d been shot. In the crotch. And the heart. And the head.

events.did: insisted that June wear her body for the gig so the man and the mistress would know exactly who was killing them
events.quote_anchor: had insisted that June wear her body for the gig, so the man and the mistress would know exactly who was killing them

events.did: read Victor's message, then buried herself inside another body and started for the door
events.quote_anchor: burying herself and her pain and her pink toes inside another body as she started for the door

relations.did: Victor had been pinging June with sonar pings that went silent for months, and now he sent her a text
relations.quote_anchor: His sonar pings had petered out these last few months, as if he understood that she’d gone off the board.

relations.did: the wife hired June to do the killing in the wife's own body
relations.quote_anchor: The wife had found out what she was, what she could do, had insisted that June wear her body for the gig

relations.did: the mistress was a different woman from the wife, the one lying on the penthouse rug
relations.quote_anchor: The wife, not to be confused with the mistress ruining the rug.

relations.did: the news that Syd had been taken sank through June and put her in motion immediately
relations.quote_anchor: June took up the phone, and stared at the text, the message sinking through her like a stone.

numbers.did: how long she slept in the penthouse: eight hours
numbers.quote_anchor: Eight hours on eight-hundred thread-count sheets did wonders for a person’s mood.

numbers.did: the thread count of the sheets: eight-hundred
numbers.quote_anchor: Eight hours on eight-hundred thread-count sheets did wonders for a person’s mood.

numbers.did: how long ago she had been shot: more than a year
numbers.quote_anchor: It had been more than a year since she’d been shot, but June had since discovered, much to her chagrin, that her body only healed while she was wearing it.

numbers.did: the length of the message he sent June: three words
numbers.quote_anchor: the message opened. It was three words long.

numbers.did: the number of coats of polish she was about to apply: a second
numbers.quote_anchor: She was about to apply a second coat when her phone chimed on the nearby counter.
